title: Cost Sensitivity Heatmap + Safe Rollback Wizard for Batch/Cache Recommendations
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design a new Console widget and accompanying wizard to help operators evaluate, simulate, and safely apply batching & prefix/KV cache recommendations. The feature centers on a cost-sensitivity heatmap that visualizes how throughput, cache hit rate, and batching thresholds change per-token cost and latency SLO risk, plus a Safe Rollback Wizard that generates an incremental rollout plan with automatic guardrails and a canary rollback checklist. Deliverables: hi-fi Figma screens (widget + expanded panel + wizard), microcopy for tooltips and guardrails, interaction spec for simulation controls, and a developer handoff artifact with variables for binding to runtime metrics. This ticket covers design, prototype testing with a solutions engineer, and consolidation of review feedback for handoff to ENG and PM.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap UI shows cost delta (%) and expected P95 latency impact for configurable axes: request rate, batch size, cache hit rate.
Simulation controls let user toggle live metrics vs. synthetic scenarios and preview token cost trend and latency percentiles.
Safe Rollback Wizard outputs a stepwise plan: canary percent, monitoring windows, automatic fallback model variants, and suggested throttles with clear rationale.
All microcopy meets accessibility/readability standards and includes clear rationale links to the recommendation engine and rollout policies.
Design files (Figma) and a compact spec (Confluence) are linked in the ticket and pass PM and ENG review comments.
Prototype tested with 3 ops/platform engineers and at least two design adjustments incorporated.
Edge-case behaviour (zero cache hits, burst traffic) documented and annotated in handoff.
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Torres): emphasize 'cost delta' vs 'absolute cost' in legend; add quick link to billing insights.
Eng (Riley Zhang): add an events contract for simulation toggles; prefer explicit rate buckets rather than continuous slider for deterministic load tests.
Security (Joan Li): confirm no sensitive customer identifiers shown in expanded simulation logs; approve as long as telemetry is anonymized.

acceptance_test_steps: Load demo dataset and enable simulation mode; verify heatmap responds to selecting 'burst + cold cache' scenario.
Apply a recommended batch size change via wizard in a staging org; confirm generated canary schedule and that fallback triggers produce expected UI state.
Run accessibility linting on tooltips and verify color contrast for heatmap buckets.
Validate telemetry events emitted for each simulation and rollback action (event names documented in Confluence).
notes: Trade-offs: a continuous slider is more discoverable but nondeterministic for SREs; we chose discrete buckets for reproducible simulation runs.
We scoped out a server-side autosuggest for guardrail thresholds to keep initial rollout schedule modest; can be added in a follow-up.
If rollout metrics show more than 10% P95 latency increase in canary, the wizard will recommend immediate rollback and provide a one-click revert option.
